title: Memory Symphony: budget ledger and dynamic headroom for KV-aware continuous batching
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Design and implement a lightweight in-memory budgeting ledger that continuously tracks and enforces memory reservations across model weights, KV cache, and transient activations for inference workers. The ledger will support policy-driven headroom targets per worker class, soft preemption hints, and a feedback loop from KV pressure signals to batching rate controls. Goal: reduce OOM risk and tail latency spikes while preserving throughput and minimizing additional allocation overhead.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime maintains a measurable headroom percentage (configurable, default 8%) across 99th percentile multi-tenant traces without OOMs for 72-hour soak. 2) Continuous batching latency p95 for interactive workloads changes less than 5% vs baseline when ledger is enabled. 3) KV pressure events decrease by at least 30% in mixed small/long-seq workloads. 4) Feature gated and rolloutable via runtime-1.20 with metrics surfaced in Console.
implementation_notes:
- Introduce a compact ledger structure (per-worker) storing reserved_weight_bytes, reserved_kv_bytes, reserved_activation_bytes, and soft_headroom_target as 64-bit counters encoded in a contiguous buffer to avoid GC churn.
- Expose a tight contract for callers: ReserveForRequest(request_signature, estimate) -> ReservationToken or RetryHint. ReservationToken must be cheap to apply to actual allocations and released deterministically.
- Integrate KV pressure sensor: when KV eviction rate or miss ratio exceeds thresholds, emit a rate-limit hint to the batching controller and reduce batch formation aggressiveness for tails.
- Provide a conservative fallback policy: if an eviction cascade is detected, automatically reduce live batch concurrency and prioritize short sequences.
- Data structures must be lock-free or use sharded atomics to keep critical path < 200ns per allocation.
- Add a simulation harness (see links) to model mixed tenant footprints and validate headroom policies before rollout.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag off by default in runtime-1.20.
2) Canary: enable on 1% of serving capacity in staging with synthetic traffic that stresses KV.
3) Metrics verification for 48h (no increased OOMs, acceptable latency deltas).
4) Ramp to 10% then 50% with manual checkpoints.
5) Full rollout when stable for 7 days and cost delta within target.
6) Provide escape hatch toggles and automated rollback on severity-level alerts.
risks: incorrect static estimates cause over-reservation and throughput regression
race conditions in ledger updates could cause stale headroom values
edge workloads (very long sequences) might still saturate memory despite headroom; needs special handling
increased CPU overhead in allocation hot path if not carefully optimized
test_plan: unit tests for ledger allocate/release semantics including concurrent reservations
integration test with KV emulator and synthetic mixed-tenant traffic
soak test on staging fleet for 72 hours with 10,000 concurrent streams
fuzz test for reservation token lifecycle and faulty releases
